The primary relationship between the modifications is that the removal of the power domain specification in `bcm2835-common.dtsi` is a direct response to the instability issues encountered with the register-based driver for the V3D component. This change is part of a broader effort to revert to a more stable firmware-based power management approach.

The inclusion of `bcm2835-rpi-common.dtsi` in `bcm2837.dtsi`, `bcm2835.dtsi`, and `bcm2836.dtsi` suggests an effort to standardize and share common configurations across different device tree files for various Raspberry Pi models, ensuring that they all benefit from the same set of definitions and configurations. Here is the commit message:
ARM: dts: bcm283x: Use firmware PM driver for V3D

The register based driver turned out to be unstable, specially on RPi3a+
but not limited to it. While a fix is being worked on, we roll back to
using firmware based scheme.

Fixes: e1dc2b2e1bef ("ARM: bcm283x: Switch V3D over to using the PM driver instead of firmware")
Signed-off-by: Nicolas Saenz Julienne <nsaenzjulienne@suse.de>
Tested-by: Stefan Wahren <stefan.wahren@i2se.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200303173217.3987-1-nsaenzjulienne@suse.de

Here is the root cause:
The instability of the register-based power management driver for the V3D component, particularly on the Raspberry Pi 3a+ and potentially other models, led to the decision to revert to a firmware-based power management scheme until a fix for the driver can be implemented.

Here is the patch:
 			reg = <0x7ec00000 0x1000>;
 			interrupts = <1 10>;
-			power-domains = <&pm BCM2835_POWER_DOMAIN_GRAFX_V3D>;
 		};
